To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fibronectin-dependent upregulation and activation of matrix metalloprotease production in hepatic stel-late cells is mediated through integrin receptors, and it involves tyro-sine phosphorylation dependent signalling pathways.
the upregulation of gelatinase production in HSCs is a marker function of FN dependent activation and transition of HSC to MFB like cells.

fibronectin dependent transition of hepatic fibroblasts to myofiboblasts is mediated through fibronectin receptor, alpha5beta1 and that the transition involves tyrosine kinase dependent signaling pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the FN-dependent up-regulation of MMPs by HSCs and its possible involvement in the activation and proliferation of HSCs.
the FN-dependent up-regulation of matrix metallopeptidase production by HCSs.
the role of FN and integrins in the activation of HSCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FN-dependent transition of quiescent HSCs to MFB-like cells is mediated through integrin signaling pathways, which in turn upregulates MMP production by the activated HSCs.
FN dependent transition of quiescent HSCs to activated MFB-like cells may occur through the upregulation of metalloproteinases.
FN-dependent upregula-tion of MMPs in HSCs is integrin mediated and involves tyrosine kinase dependent signal transduction pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FN-dependent activation of HSCs involves integrins, tyrosine phosphorylating pathways and MMPs, and these pathways may be involved in the activation and transition of HSC into MFB-like cells.
FN-dependent activation of MMPs by HSCs is a marker function of HSCs transition to MFBs and that it may be mediated through alpha5beta1 FN receptor.
FN-dependent upregu-lation of MMPs in HSCs is a marker function and it is mediated through integrin signaling pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FN-induced upregulation of gelatinase production in HSCs is dependent upon integrins and tyrosine kinase signaling pathways.
the FN-dependent transition to a myofibroblastic phenotype in HSCs may be due to the upregulation of a matrix metalloproteinase, which is a key enzyme in extracellular matrix remodeling.
the transition of quiescent HSCs to activated HSCs is influenced by FN.
